$comment: The release ledger for event contracts. A schema file is RELEASED only in the phase that gains a real producer for it, because a released file is immutable (ADR-0026) and freezing a contract nobody has exercised guarantees a .v2 later. It lives beside events/ rather than inside it because codegen globs that directory. Digests are checked by tests/contract/test_event_schemas.py, so editing a released schema fails the build unless the digest is deliberately updated here -- which makes the change visible in review.

components.note: Shared $ref, not a topic. Every released event embeds it.

released.key_reason: identity changes must order against that account's transactions
device-sharing detection is order-sensitive on the device, not the account
one message exists per case, and the case is the entity that exists at produce time; an investigation_id is minted later by the worker that leases it (ADR-0027)
released.cleanup_reason: MUST NOT be compacted. Compaction retains only the newest record per KEY, and the key is case_id -- so a reopened case (Phase 5 /v1/investigations/{id}/reopen) would silently erase the original request and every historical request but the last. The key is for routing and ordering, not identity: identity is event_id, which is unique per event.

released.key_reason: the only reader is a per-account window, so per-account order is the order that matters; equal partitions to tx.raw.v1 put an account on the same partition number on both topics (ADR-0049)
released.producer: data.generator (eval-v2 outcome stream) and trace-gateway POST /v1/events/authorization (transactional outbox)

planned.note: Deferred from Phase 2 to Phase 3 by approved decision. A topic is released only in the phase that gains a real producer for it (docs/EVENT_CONTRACTS.md §3), and the gateway cannot publish it until Kafka lands: writing a scored row per transaction to the outbox instead would put Postgres on the hot path for the ~97% of traffic that opens no case, against ADR-0002.
